note: Rewritten from the species-level description of Anenteotermes improcinctus in Sands (1972), original in English; the species has no soldiers; measurement-table headings, figure numbers, type locality and collection records are not translated; several OCR-corrupted figures in the measurement table are omitted; the name of the further allied species in the comparison sentences is spelled inconsistently in the OCR, so only the morphological differences are retained and the name is omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: One of the three smallest species of the genus, only A. nanus being smaller; compared with A. nanus, the alate has the first marginal tooth of the right mandible shorter than the second, both castes have longer mandibular apical teeth, and the worker enteric valve bears appendages. A. polyscolus is similar in size, but its alate has a larger and more conspicuous fontanelle and felt-like pilosity, both castes have longer apical teeth, and its enteric valve characters are also readily recognized. In the other, larger species the alate has a weaker meso- and metanotal constriction and the worker a shorter mixed segment. The worker abdomen appears to be of the dehiscent type.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule yellowish white, pilosity sparse, fine, yellow. Postclypeus rather strongly inflated, Pcl/W 0.35–0.36, Pcl/Ri 2.66–3.00. Mandibular apical teeth short, La/Li 0.61–0.63, Ra/Ri 0.77–0.78; the accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible just clears the molar prominence in surface view, composite ratio 17.87–18.52; the first marginal tooth of the right mandible lies distinctly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, its anterior margin shorter than that of the second marginal tooth, composite ratio 20.90–21.10. Fore tibia moderately inflated, T1/Tw 3.85–4.00, the third apical spur short, about one third the length of the other two. The midgut-hindgut overlap is about four times the midgut width at the attachment of the Malpighian tubules, or slightly less; the enteric valve seating is almost unlobed, nearly a ring, sessile on the second hindgut pouch, dorsolateral in the unopened abdomen; the enteric valve cushions are entirely retracted and of roughly equal development, with only a scaly surface; the membranous wall between the cushions and outside them bears very sparse minute spines.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule dark brown, darker above the ocelli; fontanelle very small, long oval, flat or slightly concave, brown, nearly absent in some specimens; the median spot also very small, long oval, flat, concolorous with the head capsule; postclypeus brown, labrum pale yellowish brown; frontal mark smooth, flat, semicircular, concolorous with the head capsule; antennae pale brown to brown. Pronotum and meso- and metanotal plates brown, transverse sutures present; femora and tibiae pale brown, tarsi pale yellow. Abdominal tergites and dorsal pleural spiracles brown, sternites pale brown and paler medially, ventral pleural spiracles pale; cerci pale yellowish brown. Posterior margin of head capsule evenly rounded; ocelli rather small, separated from the slightly flattened compound eye by one quarter to slightly more than one third their own minimum diameter; postclypeus rather strongly inflated, Pcl/W 0.30–0.34, posterior margin evenly rounded, median suture distinct only in the middle. Mandibular apical teeth short, La/Li 0.50–0.60, Ra/Ri 0.67–0.86; the accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible just clears the molar prominence in surface view, composite ratio 11.42–12.91; the first marginal tooth of the right mandible lies only slightly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, the anterior margins of the marginal teeth about equal, composite ratio 26.00–30.00. Head capsule pilosity uneven, yellow, not felt-like.
